question: Who chaired the commission that drafted the Indian Penal code which was enacted in 1860?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Macaulay**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Macaulay** chaired the commission that drafted the Indian Penal Code, which was enacted in 1860.
 
• The Indian Penal Code (IPC) is the official criminal code of India, covering all substantive aspects of criminal law.
 
• It was drafted in 1860 on the recommendations of the first law commission of India established in 1834 under the Charter Act of 1833 under the chairmanship of Lord Macaulay.
 
• The IPC has since been amended several times and is now supplemented by other criminal provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Babington Macaulay**, commonly known as Lord Macaulay, was a British historian and politician.
 
• He played a significant role in the introduction of English and Western concepts to education in India.
 
• His efforts laid the groundwork for the modern Indian legal system, and the IPC remains a cornerstone of Indian law to this day.
 
• The IPC is divided into 23 chapters, comprising 511 sections, and is applicable to the whole of India except the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
